newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips end slightly higher after posting big gains.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips end slightly higher after posting big gains.

text.p: Stocks ended modestly higher Wednesday after an early rally sparked by surprisingly good news on wholesale prices fell prey to profit-taking ahead of Thursday's report on consumer prices.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 11.95 points at 7,286.16, which was just shy of Monday's record finish of 7,292.75.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,473 to 993 on active volume of 489 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Blue chips romped ahead from the start with the Dow surging more than 75 points on news that the Producer Price Index for April posted its biggest drop in nearly four years, falling 0.6 percent.
The Labour Department's report signalled an economy that continues to grow with few signs of outright inflation.
It was the fourth straight month that producer prices have fallen and followed a 0.1 percent slide in March.
Analysts said the big drop in the producer prices lowered the odds that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates at next Tuesday's policy-setting meeting.
But investors turned cautious and took profits, realising that a good producer price report did not necessarily bode for a similar consumer price figure.
"When you get these oddball moves in PPI, they're not usually replicated in CPI. It takes a lot more to tug CPI from its underlying trend," said Fred Sturm, economist at Fuji Securities Inc.
Economists expect the CPI to show an April increase of 0.1 percent after a similar rise in March.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond jumped half a point, lowering its yield to 6.88 percent from Tuesday's 6.93 percent. The bond's price and yield move in opposite directions.

"If (Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan) wants to be pre-emptive against inflation and sneak some tightenings in before the next downturn, he's going to do it even if this week's data is benign," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management division.
Although some Wall Streeters may be bracing for another rise in interest rates next week, analysts remains confident that the Fed is not about to embark on a long-term cycle of rate increases.
"The Fed is going to be hard-pressed to continue raising rates," said Edward Yardeni, chief economist for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Yardeni said he had just raised his year-end Dow target to 8,000 from 7,600.

Interest-rate sensitive bank stocks surged amid the benign inflation news and strong bond market. J.P. Morgan & Co. jumped 2-1/2 to 104-1/2, BankAmerica Corp. rose 4 to 120-7/8, and Citicorp added 2-3/8 to 120-1/2.

Intel Corp. rose 3/8 to 152-3/4, a slight rebound from Tuesday's steep losses after the chipmaker said its technology did not violate any patents and it would vigorously defend itself in a patent infringment lawsuit filed by rival Digital Equipment Corp., whose stock was off 5/8 at 34-5/8.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 1.96 points to 1,335.55.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks was up 2.91 to 836.04. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.37 to 581.97.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.63 to 435.60. The average share was up 16 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,874.563 up 25.347 or 0.32 percent.
